rows.text: Pair creation and annihilation convert energy between photons and particle rest mass. Threshold energy and momentum conservation determine what processes are allowed.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Electron rest energy mec²=0.511 MeV; pair threshold=1.022 MeV.
Pair-production energy balance: Eγ=2mec²+Kpair+Knucleus.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Particle-Antiparticle Annihilation:** When a particle meets its antiparticle (e.g., $e^- + e^+$), they annihilate into pure energy (photons). Total mass-energy is conserved: $2m_e c^2 = 2 \times 0.511$ MeV = 1.022 MeV of gamma rays. Charge, lepton number, and momentum are also conserved.  ·  **Pair Production (Creation):** The reverse of annihilation: a high-energy photon ($E > 1.022$ MeV) creates an $e^- e^+$ pair near a nucleus (to conserve momentum). The photon must have $E \ge 2m_e c^2$. Excess energy becomes kinetic energy of the pair.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A single photon cannot create a pair in free space while conserving momentum.  ·  The 1.022 MeV threshold is specific to an electron–positron pair.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: At-rest e⁻e⁺ annihilation gives two opposite 0.511 MeV photons.  ·  A 1.50 MeV photon leaves at most 0.478 MeV for pair kinetic energy and nuclear recoil.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Creation and annihilation convert rest mass into photons and photons into a pair, when energy and momentum can both be conserved. An electron and a positron at rest annihilate into at least two photons whose energies total 1.022 MeV. That is a different energy ledger from the 200 MeV of a fission.  ·  The working relations are An electron and a positron annihilate into photons and The rest energy of an electron is 511 keV. Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Annihilation occurs when a particle meets its antiparticle; rest mass may convert to photons while energy, momentum and charge remain conserved. For an electron and positron initially at rest, two photons travel in opposite directions so total momentum is zero.  ·  An electron rest energy is mec²=0.511 MeV. An at-rest electron–positron pair can produce two 0.511 MeV photons, total energy 1.022 MeV.  ·  Pair production is the reverse: a sufficiently energetic photon creates an electron and positron near a nucleus. The nucleus recoils, allowing momentum conservation; one photon cannot create the pair in empty space while conserving both energy and momentum.

rows.text: A special case, such as a right angle or a steady temperature, has to be stated before it is used.  ·  An electron and a positron annihilate at rest. Find the total photon energy. Use 511 keV for each rest energy.  ·  The photon threshold is at least 2mec²=1.022 MeV. Any energy above threshold becomes kinetic energy of the pair and recoil.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Creation/annihilation of particle–antiparticle pairs is distinct from nuclear fission and fusion, although all processes obey mass-energy conservation.
